subject: royal crown
title: The 5 Youngest Monarchs Ever, Ranked (#1 Wasn't Born Yet)

scenes.text: The five youngest monarchs in history. Number one was crowned before he was born.
Number five: Henry the Sixth of England. King at about nine months old.
scenes.label: Henry VI · 9 months

scenes.text: Number four: Sobhuza the Second of Swaziland. King at about four months, and he reigned eighty-two years.
scenes.label: Sobhuza II · 4 months

scenes.text: Number three: Mary, Queen of Scots. Queen at just six days old.
scenes.label: Mary of Scots · 6 days

scenes.text: Number two: Alfonso the Thirteenth of Spain. His father died before he was born, so he was king the moment he arrived.
scenes.label: Alfonso XIII · 0 days

scenes.text: Number one: Shapur the Second of Persia. Legend says the crown was placed on his mother's belly. Then he ruled seventy years.
scenes.label: Shapur II · before birth

description:
The five youngest monarchs, ranked by age on becoming monarch.
Henry VI became king of England at about nine months; Sobhuza II of Swaziland at about four months; Mary, Queen of Scots at six days; Alfonso XIII of Spain was king from birth after his father's death; and legend says Persia's Shapur II was crowned in the womb before reigning about 70 years (309 to 379).
Who would you put at number one?
first_comment: Which would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
